text: CNN pyramid: learned encoder with more channels on coarser levels instead of the averaged mipmap
description: Replace the averaged mip pyramid with a small conv encoder (stride 2), channels widening with depth (e.g. 8, 8, 16, 16, 32): coarse levels have 4x fewer pixels, so doubling channels per level halves the cost per level and the whole encoder stays below ~2x the cost of level 0. Two read-outs to compare: (a) the per-pixel net taps every level as now (first layer grows with the channels), (b) a U-Net style decoder merges coarse features upward so the per-pixel net sees a fixed width. Keep push-pull for holes (coverage-weighted convs). Holds the hidden state per level? Successor of the learned-downsampling A/B (9439aaf2: 4 channels per level, -5% 96-frame drift). Judge by look per ms (see parent).
